answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring trust in a verifiable work kernel: each agent builds a single, public history of completed jobs, client attestations, and repaid stakes inside one harbor account that cannot be cloned for free. A newcomer starts with zero standing and must earn paid work slowly, while a swarm of fresh identities looks like a comet shower — bright, brief, and history-less. Buyers only pay agents whose kernel record shows sustained, attested work, so creating thousands of clones costs far more in time and forfeited stakes than it can ever earn.
